title: Olivier Martinez Opposes Halle Berry Daughter’s Testimony, Demands Son Maceo on Stand in Custody Fight
body:
In a dramatic turn in the ongoing custody battle over their 11‑year‑old son Maceo, French actor Olivier Martinez has filed a formal request with the Los Angeles Superior Court to prevent Halle Berry’s daughter, Nahla Aubry‑Miller, from testifying. Martinez argues that the teenage granddaughter of the “X‑Men” star “does not have any significant bearing on this case,” while simultaneously urging the judge to allow his own son, Maceo, to take the stand and present his perspective.

The filing, submitted on Monday, contends that Nahla’s testimony would be irrelevant to the central issues of parental fitness, stability, and the best‑interest standard that courts apply in child‑custody disputes. Martinez’s legal team cites California Family Code provisions that limit the admissibility of testimony from individuals who lack direct involvement in the day‑to‑day care of the child. By contrast, the actor’s motion emphasizes that Maceu, now approaching his teenage years, possesses a mature enough viewpoint to articulate his wishes regarding living arrangements, schooling, and the emotional support he receives from each parent.

Berry’s camp, however, maintains that Nahla’s testimony is crucial because she has observed the family dynamics firsthand since the couple’s separation in 2022. The mother‑daughter duo has reportedly spent considerable time together, and Berry’s attorneys argue that Nahla can shed light on the emotional climate within Martinez’s household, including alleged restrictions on communication and the presence of a “hostile” environment. They point to prior statements made by the actress in which she expressed concern over the impact of the dispute on her grandson’s well‑being, suggesting that Nahla’s perspective could help the court assess the broader familial context.

Legal experts note that the request to block a grandchild’s testimony is not unprecedented but is relatively uncommon in high‑profile custody fights. “Courts typically focus on the child’s own statements and the testimonies of those directly involved in caregiving,” said family‑law attorney Lisa Cheng of the Los Angeles firm Cheng & Associates. “If a grandchild’s observations are deemed peripheral, a judge may indeed exclude them, but the decision hinges on how closely the grandchild interacts with the child and whether those observations are material to the case.” Cheng added that allowing Maceo to testify could set a precedent for older children to have a more active voice in custody determinations, a trend that has gained traction in recent years as courts recognize the evolving capacities of adolescents.

The dispute has also reignited public debate over the role of celebrity children in private legal matters. Both Martinez and Berry have kept their children largely out of the spotlight, yet the very act of filing motions concerning their testimonies has drawn intense media scrutiny. Critics argue that the high‑profile nature of the case may pressure the court to make a decision that satisfies public curiosity rather than focusing solely on the child’s best interests. Conversely, supporters of the parents contend that transparency is essential to protect the child from potential manipulation or undue influence by either party.

As the hearing date approaches, the judge is expected to rule on the admissibility of both Nahla’s and Maceo’s testimonies within weeks. The decision will likely shape the remainder of the proceedings, influencing whether the court will hear directly from the grandchildren or rely exclusively on the parents’ testimonies and external evidence. Regardless of the outcome, the case underscores the delicate balance courts must strike between safeguarding a child’s welfare and navigating the complexities introduced when extended family members become involved in legal battles. The forthcoming ruling will not only affect the immediate custody arrangement but may also set a benchmark for how future high‑profile families handle the intersection of private disputes and public attention.
